Voted “Best Food Truck in Denver” by 5280 Magazine, our hearty bowls will fill you up
without bogging you down. Crock Spot Gourmet Food Trucks and Catering offers the
Denver Metro area slow-cooked goodness. All of our proteins, including our vegetarian &
vegan options, are cooked slowly to mouthwatering perfection, served over healthy grain
varietals and topped with an international sauce of choice.
Our “quick serve” concept makes sure our guests never wait in a long line. Our team can
have a guest served in 25 seconds or less, which makes our cuisine ideal for any time
sensitive event. Our unique concept invites our customers to “choose their own adventure”
when ordering.

CLEAR SPACE

All other content near the logo should at least
be a minimum distance of the height of the

COLORS
Do not alter logo colors.
OTHER ALTERATIONS
Do not add a stroke or heavy drop shadow around the logo.
PROPORTIONS
Never alter the original proportions of the logo
by stretching, squishing, or skewing it.
SIZING

Avoid losing legibility.

Photography
PHOTOGRAPHIC STYLE
Photography should be fun, bright, and full of color. Subject matter should be food and service
focused and include images of happy customers. Ideally, the hues within the photos should include
touches of the purple, green, red, and gold from the brand palette.
10
Copy standards
EDITORIAL STYLE
• Don’t use quotation marks when quoting song lyrics.
• Pun hard and pun often.
• Use exclamation points to enhance copy. Use sparingly and never
more than one at a time.
• Use all capital letters to emphasize some words as needed. Never
use two all capital words in the same sentence.
TAGLINES/PUNS

Crock It Like Its Hot
11
messaging
VOICE
• Authentic and approachable
• Warm and inviting
• Fun and friendly
• Simple and conversational
TONE
Crock Spot’s tone is friendly and conversational. Maintain a casual
tone while fitting in “crock” puns wherever possible.
When writing short taglines and sayings, use popular lyrics with
“crock” in place of a word in a rock song.
Ex: We will, we will, CROCK you.
Ex: Let’s give them something to CROCK about.
When describing the food, maintain an informative and fun tone
while describing flavors.
Ex: A fan favorite! Sriracha is an Asian hot sauce made from chili
paste. We mix it with sour cream for a MEDIUM heat sauce.
12
Customer personas
CUSTOMER 1
Kelly is a 39-year-old woman with two kids aged 13 and 9. She
values eateries that allow her and her children to customize their
own meals while still being quick and healthy. Her 13-year-old has a
gluten allergy and she prefers to eat vegan meals whenever possible.
CUSTOMER 2
Josh is a 25-year-old business development representative at
a software start up. He goes out to lunch with coworkers every
weekday and prefers places that have healthier options and a lot
of variety. He’s a busy guy, so he prefers fast casual but is tired of
burritos and pizza all the time.
CUSTOMER 3
Pierce is a 30-year-old barista who loves to travel and try new
things. He prefers healthy options and enjoys trying new foods from
different cultures. He enjoys a fancy dinner but is budget conscious
so he tends to eat at affordable, fast-casual restaurants.

March 16, 2026

Exchange Club of Murray

Murray, Utah

Re: Balloon Palooza Event -- A Statement from the Murray Area Chamber of Commerce Board of Directors

Dear Members of the Exchange Club,

On behalf of the Murray Area Chamber of Commerce Board of Directors, I am writing to formally address a matter that arose during last year's Balloon Palooza event. We understand that concerns have been raised regarding an interpersonal exchange that occurred between a chamber representative and members of a youth group in attendance. We take this matter seriously, and we want to be transparent about how we have responded.

While the board was not directly present during this interaction, we have made every effort to gather a thorough understanding of the situation. From what has been shared with us, it appears that frustration developed over adherence to event guidelines, and that an exchange took place that was more heated than any of us would consider appropriate for a public event involving young people. We recognize that regardless of the circumstances that led to the moment, the manner in which the situation was handled fell short of the standard we hold for all who represent our organization.

The board has addressed this matter directly and thoroughly. Conversations have taken place at both the individual and organizational level to ensure that all chamber representatives understand the expectations we carry into every community interaction, especially those involving youth. We have also reviewed our event volunteer protocols and communications to make certain that expectations for participants are clearly stated well in advance of future events. It is our firm commitment that situations of this nature will not be repeated.

Our Commitment to Murray Youth

We want to take this opportunity to reaffirm something that is central to who we are as an organization: the Murray Area Chamber of Commerce is deeply and genuinely committed to the young people of our community. Our ongoing relationship with the Murray Youth Community Council (MYCC) is one we are proud of and one we actively nurture. The leadership, civic engagement, and character development that the MYCC fosters in our young people reflects exactly the kind of community investment that the chamber stands behind.

That commitment is not merely stated in words. The chamber has continued to contribute scholarship funds to Murray youth as a direct and tangible expression of our belief in their potential. We have done so in the past, we are doing so now, and we intend to continue doing so going forward. The young people of Murray are not an afterthought to our mission. They are a core part of why this chamber exists.

We are grateful for the relationship we share with the Exchange Club and for your role in building the fabric of this community. It is because of that shared mission that we felt it important to address this matter directly and with full accountability. If you have questions or would like to speak further, please do not hesitate to reach out.

Respectfully,

Brett Lechtenberg

Chairman of the Board

Murray Area Chamber of Commerce
